overall: The AG found the Bristol County Commissioners violated the Open Meeting Law only by posting an 'Employment Matters' agenda item too vague to inform the public; the payroll/warrant and surety bond items were adequately detailed.

allegations.summary: Alleged that the posted notice's 'Employment Matters' item for the January 31 meeting was too vague to inform the public.
allegations.key_passage: A topic of “Employment Matters” is too broad to give a member of the public a reasonable understanding of what the public body will address.

allegations.summary: Alleged that the notice item 'Review and approve Payroll/AP Warrants' was insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: With respect to “Review and approve Payroll/AP Warrants,” we find that the notice was sufficiently detailed.

allegations.summary: Alleged that three notice items listing surety bonds (County Treasurer, Frederick M. Kalisz, John Collias) were insufficiently detailed.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we conclude that these items were sufficiently detailed.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law (G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25).
remedy_passage: We order the Commissioners’ immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
